bib.title: MemAgent: Reshaping Long-Context LLM with Multi-Conv RL-based Memory Agent

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "MemAgent: Reshaping Long-Context LLM with Multi-Conv RL-based Memory Agent". Hongli Yu, Tinghong Chen, Jiangtao Feng, Jiangjie Chen, Weinan Dai, Qiying Yu, Ya-Qin Zhang, Wei-Ying Ma, Jingjing Liu, Mingxuan Wang (corr.), Hao Zhou (corr.). Affiliations: Institute for AI Industry Research (AIR), Tsinghua University; ByteDance Seed; SIA-Lab of Tsinghua AIR and ByteDance Seed. Venue: "Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026"; arXiv:2507.02259v2 [cs.CL], dated 29 Jul 2026 in the PDF header. Year 2025 (v1), ICLR 2026.

COVERAGE: All 29 of 29 pages; 91,358 chars extracted. Read the body (pp.1-11), the appendices A-F (prompts, algorithm, training, eval, compute, case study, RAG/Mem0 tables, failure patterns) and the Figure 5/8 heatmap numbers. Skimmed the reference list only for origins. Not read line by line: the numeric heatmap rows in Fig 5/8 beyond the summary rows. No figure-image check was run; the text extraction was clean.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Mechanism: the model reads a long document chunk by chunk and OVERWRITES a fixed-length memory (ordinary tokens in the context window) after each chunk. Compute is linear and the context window is constant.
  number: 1024-token memory, 5000-token chunk, 8K window
  setup: Qwen2.5-7B/14B-Instruct backbones, no architecture change
  quote: "After reading a new chunk, the model overwrites the previous memory with an updated one. This overwrite strategy seems almost too simple, yet it is precisely what enables the system to scale: because memory length never grows, the total compute per chunk stays O(1) and end-to-end complexity is strictly linear to the number of chunks."
  where: p.3, section 2.1
- Headline extrapolation: trained on up to 60K-token documents with an 8K window, it scores 71.09 (14B) and 71.88 (7B) at 3.5M tokens on RULER-HQA, against 80.47 and 81.25 at 7K. The abstract says the loss is under 10%.
  setup: RULER-HQA, sub-EM accuracy, 128 synthetic test samples per length from the HotpotQA validation split
  quote: "being able to extrapolate from an 8K context to a 3.5M QA task with a performance loss of less than 10% and achieving over 95% on the 512K NIAH test." Table 1 row: "RL-MEMAGENT-14B 80.47 82.03 82.03 83.59 81.25 77.34 79.69 75.78 78.91 71.09"
  where: abstract p.1; Table 1 p.5
- Baselines collapse with length on RULER-HQA. Qwen2.5-Instruct-14B-1M goes 60.16 at 7K to 0.00 at 896K. QwenLong-L1-32B goes 72.66 at 7K to 11.72 at 896K. Baselines have no 1.75M or 3.5M entries (N/A).
  quote: "The Qwen2.5-Instruct-1M series maintains acceptable performance up to 112K tokens, but the performance deteriorates to zero at 896K tokens, well before reaching their theoretical 1M token capacity."
  where: p.7, section 3.2; Table 1
- RL is essential. MemAgent with the same workflow but no RL beats its backbone yet still degrades with length. On LongBench-QA, applying it without RL gives "only marginal or even negative improvements".
  number: no numeric table (Figs 5, 6, 7 only). On NIAH-Average at 512K, 14B w/o RL is 40.10, 7B w/o RL is 88.54, 32B w/o RL is 71.88, RL-14B is 98.18, RL-7B is 96.62.
  quote: "indicating reinforcement learning training is essential to develop generalizable and robust memory abilities."
  where: p.8, 3.3.1; Fig 5 averages
- NIAH: RL-MemAgent loses under 5% at 512K, which involves more than 100 dialogue turns.
  setup: RULER niah_single 1/2/3 (repeat haystack and number needle; essay haystack and number needle; essay haystack and UUID needle). Answer prefix omitted. Qwen2.5-Instruct-14B-1M and 7B-1M are strong baselines (100 at levels 1 and 2, 93.23 and 73.44 average at 512K).
  quote: "RL-MEMAGENT, despite suffering some performance fluctuations, shows only a minimal performance loss of less than 5% at 512K. This robust performance is particularly noteworthy given that the evaluation at 512K involves more than 100 turns of dialogue."
  where: p.8, 3.2
- LongBench-QA, averaged over 5 tasks: MemAgent-14B 51.0 and 7B 48.2. QwenLong-L1-32B is 50.7, Qwen2.5-Instruct-14B 42.0, 14B-1M 43.0.
  quote: "MEMAGENT-14B 79.0 73.0 52.0 25.0 26.0 51.0" and "MEMAGENT-7B 74.0 69.5 47.0 21.5 29.0 48.2"
  where: Table 3, p.6
- LongBench-SUM (GovReport/QMSum, ROUGE recall): RL-MemAgent-14B average is 21.80 and 31.39, the best in both columns. Qwen2.5-Instruct-14B-1M is 19.34 and 29.84. The text says SOTA "on almost all metrics". The 7B is not best throughout (GovReport ROUGE-1 30.28 vs 33.30 for DS-Distill-7B).
  where: Table 2, p.6
- Beats RAG and Mem0 baselines. On RULER-HQA at 3.5M, 14B RAG with top-K=8 gets 64.84 vs 71.09 for MemAgent-14B. At 7K, K=8 gets 78.12 vs 80.47. On LongBench-QA, 14B RAG with the best setting (chunk 2048, K=8) averages 39.42 vs 51.00. The Mem0 baseline used GPT-5.1 with 5,000-token chunks and top 30 memories. Its numbers are not in the extracted tables, only the claim of outperformance.
  quote: "demonstrating that end-to-end RL–trained memory provides greater flexibility and coherence compared with retrieval-based strategies."
  where: App. D.2, Tables 10-11
- Training recipe: Multi-Conv DAPO treats each context-independent conversation as a training target. The reward and advantage come from the final (answer) conversation and are applied uniformly to all earlier conversations of the same sample. Reward is a rule-based exact-match verifier. Advantage is not divided by the std (as in Dr. GRPO).
  number: KL 1e-3, lr 1e-6, rollout batch 256, group size 16
  quote: "The advantage value is derived from the conversation that contains the final answer, then uniformly applied to all conversations originating from the same sample"
  where: p.4, 2.2; App. A.3
- Two-stage curriculum. Stage I: 32,768 synthetic HotpotQA/RULER-style QA instances of about 32K tokens (around 28K each, 200 articles). Stage II: 2,560 instances up to 60K tokens, from DocQA-RL-1.6K mixed with stage I data. Stage I took about 400 steps to converge. About 50% of the 80,000 candidate samples were filtered out, because Qwen2.5-7B could answer them with no context.
  where: App. A.3
- Memory size is robust. Tested 256-4096 tokens. 1024-token memory with 5000-token chunk was the "sweet spot". With total length fixed, 14B NIAH averages stay 97-100 across 512 to 4096 and LongBench-QA averages stay 48.5-51.0.
  quote: "showing that our chosen configuration constitutes a reasonable sweet spot, and that MEMAGENT's performance is robust over different memory size."
  where: p.8, 3.3.2; Tables 8-9
- Position probe: key facts at 0/20/40/80/100% positions (information-overwrite and lost-in-the-middle tests) cause no catastrophic drop. The differences from the random placement are within about +/-8 points per length. The averages are within about 3 points.
  quote: "MemAgent remains consistently robust across all patterns without exhibiting any catastrophic performance degradation."
  where: Table 4, p.10, 3.3.3
- Compute: the FLOP estimator (from verl) shows the baseline as O(n^2) and MemAgent as O(n), compared over 8K-4M. No numeric ratio is given in text. The formula uses q=1024, o=1024, N=5000.
  where: App. B, Fig 10
- Memory text is a note-taking behaviour learned by RL. Case study (14B): it stores a possibly relevant distractor entry early, stays unchanged on an irrelevant chunk, and updates when the two relevant documents appear.
  quote: "these memory behaviors are not the result of architectural attention mechanisms, but emerge as text generation abilities reinforced through RL."
  where: App. C

LIMITS
- Failure patterns (App. F) are conceded with examples:
  (1) Information overwritten. The fixed memory fills with irrelevant material, the new key fact appended at the end is truncated, and a later self-summary drops it (Turn 289-433).
  (2) Missing critical information in multi-hop. The model can't tell the first hop is relevant until the second hop appears, which comes later (Turn 143 vs 215).
  (3) Primacy bias. It anchors on an early interpretation of "country" and keeps it (Turn 1 vs 728).
- The memory is lossy and fixed-size, so one pass can discard evidence later needed. This is the cost of the overwrite strategy. There is no revisiting of earlier chunks.
- Inference is sequential: more than 100 turns at 512K. Latency is not reported, only FLOPs.
- Evaluation is mostly synthetic (RULER-HQA built from HotpotQA, NIAH). The training distribution matches RULER-HQA. LongBench tasks are short (the authors call them "relatively short but have a high information density"). Test sets are small (128 synthetic samples; LongBench numbers in 0.5 steps, which suggests about 200 items per task, though the text does not say).
- Only Qwen2.5 7B/14B backbones were trained. The 32B "w/o RL" is a no-RL variant only. No other families tested.
- The ablation without RL is shown only in figures. The paper gives no per-seed variance or confidence intervals.
- Baselines use different context configs (Table 6: 128K or 1M window, 120K to 990K input). The RAG/Mem0 comparison uses a different embedding and LLM (GPT-5.1 for Mem0), so it is not controlled.
- Code, data and weights are only promised ("will be available").
- Possible dating: the baselines are 2024-25 models (Qwen2.5, DS-R1-Distill, QwenLong-L1).
- Memory here is working memory inside one task (streaming context compression). It is not cross-session persistent agent memory, so it only partly maps to note 06's agent-memory topics.

BUILDS ON
- DAPO (Yu et al., 2025), which refines GRPO (Shao et al., 2024). Dr. GRPO (Liu et al., 2025) for dropping std normalization.
- RLVR recipe: OpenAI 2024, Guo et al. 2025 (DeepSeek-R1), Seed 2025, Jin et al. 2025 (Search-R1).
- verl / HybridFlow (Sheng et al., 2024) for the framework.
- RULER (Hsieh et al., 2024) for the NIAH and HQA synthesis. HotpotQA (Yang et al., 2018). Kamradt 2023 for NIAH. LongBench (Bai et al., 2024).
- DocQA-RL-1.6K from QwenLong-L1 (Wan et al., 2025).
- Memory lineage credited: LSTM (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber 1997), Neural Turing Machines (Graves et al. 2014), Memory Networks (Weston et al. 2014), Miller 1956. Compared against: Mem0 (Chhikara et al. 2025), MemoryBank, MEM1 (Zhou et al. 2025), Memp, RMT (Bulatov et al. 2023), Titans (Behrouz et al. 2024).
- Multi-context agent training: GiGPO (Feng et al. 2025), Agent-R1 and Search-R1, which concatenate or window.

CODE
- Prompt template (Table 5, App. A.1, p.12). Chunk-processing prompt: "You are presented with a problem, a section of an article that may contain the answer, and a previous memory. Please read the section carefully and update the memory with new information that helps to answer the problem, while retaining all relevant details from the previous memory. <problem>{prompt}</problem> <memory>{memory}</memory> <section>{chunk}</section> Updated memory:" Final prompt: "You are presented with a problem and a previous memory. Please answer the problem based on the previous memory and put the answer in \boxed{}. <problem>{prompt}</problem> <memory>{memory}</memory> Your answer:"
- Algorithm 1, Multi-conv DAPO (App. A.2). Each rollout builds h_{g,t} = h_{g,t-1} || o_{g,t} per conversation. The final response y_g = o_{g,c_g} is scored by the verifier, and r_g = r_hat_g - beta*d_g. The group is normalised and the clipped objective is averaged over G.
- Latent-variable view (Eq 4): p(x_{1:N}) = sum over m_{1:K-1} of prod_k p(c_k | m_{k-1}) p(m_k | c_k, m_{k-1}), m_0 = empty (p.5).

FIGURES (not rendered; captions from the extraction)
- Fig 1 (p.1): RULER-HQA accuracy, 7K to 3.5M. The baselines fall off, MemAgent stays flat. The fastest summary of the claim.
- Fig 2 (p.2): MemAgent workflow (chunks, memory, question, answer) versus the long-context LLM.
- Fig 3 (p.3): GRPO vs Multi-Conv DAPO. The final conversation's answer sets the reward and advantage for all earlier conversations.
- Fig 5 (p.7): NIAH heatmaps, levels 1-3 and average, for 14 models. The w/o-RL rows show the RL effect.
- Figs 6-7 (p.8): RL ablation on RULER-HQA and LongBench-QA.
- Figs 8-9 (p.9): memory-length ablation.
- Fig 10 (App. B): FLOPs, quadratic baseline vs linear MemAgent.

PROBLEMS
- pypdf printed fontTools warnings (harmless). Table text was extracted, but some rows are flattened. In the Table 1 row for RL-MemAgent-14B, the rows' bolding is lost, so values run together ("80.4782.03" in the raw text).
- The page header says arXiv v2 dated 29 Jul 2026, while the cited year is 2025 (v1, 2507.02259).
- No embedded instructions found.
